issues.legal_issue: Compensation for compulsory requisition must account for the property's potential value when that value is supported by the available material.
material_facts: The premises were requisitioned for an indefinite period.
The intended user already had an office in a neighbouring building, making the requisitioned premises specially advantageous to that user and giving the owner greater bargaining power.
The arbitrator assessed an additional 10% for potential value and related factors, but the High Court rejected that addition without giving a reason.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in disregarding the potential value; the principles for compensation under section 19 of the Defence of India Act are the same as those under section 23(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, and potential value must be evaluated on the available material.
issues.legal_principle: The compensation principles under section 19 of the Defence of India Act are the same as those under section 23(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Potentialities must be evaluated according to the circumstances and assessed as best as possible from the material available, without speculation. Vyricherla Narayana Gajapatiraju v. The Revenue Divisional Officer (1939) L.R. 66 I.A. 104 was followed.

rule.if: requisition_compensation_proceeding and (special_advantage_to_intended_user or indefinite_requisition) and potential_value_supported_by_material and potential_value_excluded_without_reason

predicates.requisition_compensation_proceeding: The dispute concerns compensation for property taken by compulsory requisition.
predicates.special_advantage_to_intended_user: The intended user would gain a special advantage from using the property.
predicates.indefinite_requisition: The property was requisitioned for an indefinite period.
predicates.potential_value_supported_by_material: Material before the decision-maker supports a finding that the property's circumstances give it additional potential value.
predicates.potential_value_excluded_without_reason: A reviewing court excluded the property's potential value without giving a reason.

issues.definition: When a requisition-compensation dispute involves supported potential value and that value was excluded without reason, the potential value must be considered.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for requisitioned premises may include a reasonable amount for use of their lift.
material_facts: The premises had a lift used by two government departments.
An overhead bridge had been constructed to provide access between the requisitioned premises and another government-occupied building.
The owner claimed compensation for the use of the lift, and the High Court had awarded a lower amount without a clear basis.
issues.conclusion: The owner's claim for lift use was not excessive in the circumstances, and the Court enhanced the total monthly compensation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the lift claim in light of its use by two government departments and the connection between the government-occupied buildings. It stated no separate statutory provision or earlier case for this assessment.

predicates.requisition_compensation_proceeding: The dispute concerns compensation for property taken by compulsory requisition.
predicates.lift_used_by_multiple_government_departm: More than one government department used the lift in the requisitioned premises.
predicates.government_buildings_connected_for_acces: A structure provided access between the requisitioned premises and another government-occupied building.

issues.definition: When requisitioned premises have a lift used by multiple government departments and government-occupied buildings are connected for access, reasonable compensation for lift use is awarded.

issues.legal_issue: A valuation based on rents for comparable premises may be upheld when the comparison is supported by the evidence and contrary expert opinion is unsupported.
material_facts: The High Court assessed compensation using rents for two nearby premises that it found comparable, with the subject premises lying between them in relative quality.
The owner's expert gave higher rental figures but did not support the opinion with reasons.
The Supreme Court found no error in the High Court's use of the average rents and its treatment of the expert evidence.
issues.conclusion: The High Court committed no error of principle in averaging the rents of the two comparable premises, and it was right not to rely on the unsupported expert opinion.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the comparison of premises based on their relative condition and found that an expert opinion unsupported by reasons did not require reliance. No statute or earlier case was cited for this evidentiary assessment.

predicates.requisition_compensation_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning the valuation of compensation for requisitioned property.
predicates.comparable_premises_support_rental_compa: Rental evidence relates to premises found sufficiently comparable to support comparison.
predicates.subject_property_quality_lies_between_co: The subject property is found to be of a quality between the comparable properties.
predicates.contrary_expert_opinion_unsupported: An expert opinion proposing a different valuation is not supported by reasons.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, a comparable-rent valuation is upheld when the comparables support the comparison, the subject property lies between them in quality, and the contrary expert opinion is unsupported.

issues.legal_issue: An objection to the admissibility of evidence cannot be raised for the first time at a later appellate stage when it was not raised before the earlier decision-makers.
material_facts: The owner challenged the admissibility of a document relied on in connection with rental evidence.
No objection to the document's admissibility had been made before either the arbitrator or the High Court.
The document was not printed in the record before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The admissibility objection could not be raised at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain a belated objection to admissibility where no objection had been made before the arbitrator or the High Court. No statute or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.requisition_compensation_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning the valuation of compensation for requisitioned property.
predicates.evidentiary_admissibility_objection: A party challenges the admissibility of evidence relied on in the proceedings.
predicates.no_objection_before_lower_decision_maker: The party did not raise the admissibility objection before the earlier decision-makers.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, an admissibility objection is not entertained when the party failed to raise it before the earlier decision-makers.
